species.name: Chiriquí harlequin frog
species.threat_summary: The decline is attributed at least partly to chytridiomycosis; warming is not shown here to be the sole cause.

scenario.title: Which option best matches the regional climate cycle?
scenario.period_note: Educational recreation set in 2015 with the 1981–2014 archive; it does not assume the species was still alive or that these data were available at the time.
scenario.question: Compare the 12 typical months of the three variables. Choose the candidate with the smallest standardized climate distance.
scenario.model_rule: Mean of the 12-month RMSE per variable divided by the reference site’s 1981–2014 monthly standard deviation; three equal weights. A teaching rule, not an ecological model.
scenario.feedback: The lowest index identifies the regional climate analogue among these three options. p-values test for trends, not suitability. Still needed: water temperature, dissolved oxygen, stream flow, chytrid fungus.
scenario.limitations: The plots and management conditions are fictional. This is not a translocation recommendation or a survival prediction.
scenario.game_assumptions: To compare climate, all candidates are assumed to have otherwise equivalent and suitable conditions; this has not been checked in the field.

key_variables.brief_favorable_conditions: Cold, well-oxygenated mountain streams (12–17 °C), continuous cloudy canopy and stable daily temperatures.
key_variables.why_these_variables: Air temperature as a stream-temperature proxy, cloudiness and thermal stability (the brief links thermal swings to chytrid outbreaks). Water temperature and oxygen are not available.
key_variables.absolute_value_caution: Montane species: the NASA grid cell is a regional average and cannot resolve mountain-stream microclimates. Prefer the change versus normal over absolute values.

survival_card.use_rule: Compare the same indicator, unit, annual aggregation and years. Values describe the historical regional grid cell, not measured physiological tolerances. A difference or an out-of-range value does not establish survival or death.
survival_card.absolute_value_caution: Montane species: the NASA grid cell is a regional average and cannot resolve mountain-stream microclimates. Prefer the change versus normal over absolute values.

requirements.value: Stream margins in cool, humid montane forest at 1,400–2,500 m; eggs and tadpoles develop in forest streams. Water temperature and oxygen were never measured.
requirements.evidence: Elevation and stream breeding are documented; the 12–17 °C water range has no source.
requirements.proxy_note: Air temperature of a 1,018 m grid cell; not stream temperature.

requirements.value: Cool, humid cloud forest; females favour shaded forest away from streams.
requirements.evidence: The habitat is described as cool, humid cloud forest; canopy cover was never quantified.
requirements.proxy_note: NASA values describe the regional grid cell, not the habitat itself.

requirements.value: No chytrid fungus (Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis); stable temperature was not shown to matter for this species.
requirements.evidence: The decline is probably linked to chytridiomycosis; habitat loss and introduced trout were also threats. A thermal-stability link is a hypothesis.
requirements.proxy_note: Monthly temperature range is a regional proxy for thermal stability.

habitat_evidence.use_rule: Ecological evidence only. Prior review labels do not validate numerical survival limits. Do not compare these prose values or indirect proxies with NASA numbers or use them as hard survival rules.
